proposal.description: The delayed PWM copy is only tracked while the supervisor is in S_RUN, so on entry to S_RUN the cycle-boundary detector compares the live PWM with a stale sample
proposal.reason: pwm_sync is the free-running oscillator, so it keeps changing outside S_RUN. On the first clock in S_RUN, a stale pwm_sync_d=1 with PWM low creates a false falling edge, and a stale 0 hides a real one. Either way the qualifying count is off by one cycle, so PGOOD asserts one switching cycle early or late after entry or re-entry into S_RUN.

proposal.description: Leaving S_RUN pauses the qualifying count instead of restarting it; only a comparator dip clears it
proposal.reason: Suppose the supervisor leaves S_RUN with the rail still in window, for example on a fault or hiccup, and later returns. The counter keeps its old value, so PGOOD reasserts as soon as run_active returns (if the count was saturated), or before a full fresh qualifying period, when it should wait PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES again.

proposal.description: PGOOD compares the counter with one less than the terminal value the counter saturates at, an off-by-one meant to make up for the counter's register delay
proposal.reason: While the rail stays good in S_RUN, PGOOD asserts one switching cycle early. It then drops when the counter steps to TARGET and stays low while the counter is saturated, so PGOOD is a single-cycle pulse and never stays high.
